blocks.text: The kinetic theory of gases describes the molecules of a gas and their motion. In this theory, the pressure of a gas arises from its particles colliding with the walls of the container. The theory also explains properties such as temperature, volume and pressure, and transport properties such as viscosity, thermal conductivity and diffusion. The kinetic molecular theory applies to ideal gases, and was introduced in the previous class. Its basic assumptions are:

items: A gas consists of a very large number of tiny particles that are far apart compared with their sizes.
Gas particles are in constant, rapid motion in random directions.
Collisions between gas particles and the container walls are perfectly elastic.
There are no forces of attraction or repulsion between gas particles except during collisions.
The average kinetic energy of the gas particles depends on the temperature of the gas.

blocks.title: Do you know?
blocks.text: A small 'cube' of air can contain as many as 10^20 molecules. The volume of the gas particles themselves is negligible compared with the volume of the empty space between them.

blocks.title: Mean free path
blocks.text: The mean free path is the average distance a moving particle covers before it undergoes a collision that significantly changes its direction or energy.
